subject: Temporary coverage letter request (post-report gap) - PrismWorks
messages:
From: Alex Stone <alex.stone@prismworks.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@prismworks.com>, security@prismworks.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary coverage letter + evidence for SOC 2 gap (post-report)

Hi Ben,

We're doing the final vendor security review for Redwood as part of PrismWorks' 2026 procurement cycle. We received the SOC 2 Type II report (period ended 2026-03-31) but need a short transitional assurance / temporary coverage letter that confirms there have been no material changes to the controls relevant to the scope since the report end date through today (target: 2026-06-15), or an explanation of compensating controls if any change occurred.

Specific asks: 
- A one-page coverage/bridge letter covering 2026-04-01 through 2026-06-15 (statement of continuity).
- Copy of the SOC 2 Type II report that you intend to rely on (we have a partial copy; can you attach the final PDF).
- Control mapping or matrix for the in-scope systems (hosted API, data storage, backup/restore).
- KMS key rotation evidence and a short incident history (since 2026-03-31).
- Confirmation of any production network or auth architecture changes since the report date.

Target: we'd like a draft by end of week (Fri 2026-06-19) so our Legal and SecOps can review ahead of an SSO integration kickoff the following week. Please advise who will be the Redwood lead and whether you need a vendor evidence checklist from us (we can provide SCP/format).

Thanks,
Alex Stone
Head of Vendor Security
PrismWorks
alex.stone@prismworks.com
+1 415-555-0192

Date: Mon, 15 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear list. Happy to help and we can get you a standard short coverage letter plus the supporting docs. Proposed plan:

1) I'll coordinate with Legal and Security and circulate a draft coverage letter by end of day Wed (2026-06-17).
2) Vivek will provide the KMS rotation evidence, control matrix extract, and a short incident summary.
3) Marissa will review/approve the legal language; we can produce a signed PDF if you need a signature on company letterhead.

Could you confirm the exact scope to cover (full hosted API + customer data stores? or limited to the public API endpoints only). Also: is the DocuSign signature required or is a signed PDF sufficient?

I've attached a short vendor-evidence checklist we use internally to speed intake.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Re: Request: temporary coverage letter + evidence for SOC 2 gap (post-report)

Alex — forwarding the ask and attaching a draft of the coverage letter for your review. I've kept the language narrow and factual; this is intended to bridge from the SOC 2 report period end (2026-03-31) to the requested coverage window (2026-04-01 through 2026-06-15). Please see the draft below and let me know if PrismWorks requires additions (e.g., reference to specific Trust Services Criteria or an explicit list of in-scope subcomponents).

Draft (suggested):
Redwood Inference confirms that, to the best of its knowledge and based on its controls and evidence, there have been no material changes to the controls relevant to the scope of the SOC 2 Type II report for the period ending March 31, 2026. This statement covers the period from April 1, 2026 through June 15, 2026. Redwood will provide the SOC 2 Type II report and supporting documentation (control matrix and KMS rotation logs) to PrismWorks for review.

If any changes are identified that materially affect the assessed controls prior to final issuance, Redwood will notify PrismWorks promptly and provide an explanation of compensating controls or remediation steps.

-- Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: coverage-letter-draft.docx
